primary_source.content: Kolkata: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Tuesday launched 'Arjun Vahini' for early-stage disaster response, initially comprising 200 personnel, primarily retired soldiers and former Agniveers.Of the 200 personnel, 100 will be deployed in Kolkata, while 50 each will be stationed in the hills and the Sundarbans, he told reporters at the state secretariat."The force will be tasked with responding to disasters and emergencies," the chief minister said.The Sunday Story | The first Agniveers are about to leave. What happens to them next?About their remuneration, Adhikari said the head of the force, 'Veer Nayak', will receive a monthly honorarium of Rs 40,000, while the other members, 'Veers', will be paid Rs 25,000."Their remuneration will increase by three per cent annually," he said, adding that the force will primarily comprise retired soldiers and former Agniveers.In the event of death while on duty, they will be provided Rs 10 lakh compensation, while Rs 5 lakh ex gratia will be paid for permanent disability, the chief minister said.Adhikari added the new force would eventually be developed along the lines of the National Disaster Response Force, with greater manpower and advanced technology to strengthen its disaster-response capabilities.

stories.primary_headline: IIT suicides: Are India's elite campuses doing enough to protect its students?

primary_source.headline: IIT suicides: Are India’s elite campuses doing enough to protect its students?
primary_source.content: For many students, getting into an Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) is supposed to be the point where years of pressure finally pays off. The ‘IIT’ tag has long been seen as a gateway to a secure future, a good job and a strong career.Inside the campus, however, that promise can look very different."Before coming to IIT, you feel you've given your best," said Piyush, a second-year BTech student at IIT Delhi. "Then you realise everyone here has been the best in their lives."The pressure isn't just exams. It's keeping up with an immensely competitive peer group, managing placements anxiety, and sometimes just finding someone to talk to.IIT Delhi forms fact-finding committee after row over discussion on caste held in campusPiyush, B.Tech II year, IIT Delhi"Before coming to IIT, you feel you've given your best. Then you realise everyone here has been the best in their lives."At least 160 student deaths have been recorded across India's top engineering colleges in two decades, with 69 in the last five alone. A separate RTI data shows 37 suicides across 11 IITs between 2019-20 and 2023-24, with IIT Madras and IIT Hyderabad reporting seven each, and IIT Delhi six.Even these numbers don't tell the full story. No single database tracks the number of student deaths across all 23 IITs. But even then, the issue remains glaring. There is a mental health crisis at India’s premium campuses and despite a number of reforms announced and implemented, it does not seem to be enough.Academic pressure: The first breaking pointFor students like Rohan (name changed), the problem starts long before a crisis."The overall curriculum, the timetable throughout the day is very hectic. And to counter that, there are little to no practical approaches," he said, adding that while the institutes offer yoga sessions, clubs and cultural activities to support student well-being, students often don't have time to take part."If students have to pull all-nighters to accommodate everything they want to do, their personal life, their academics and their social life, then there is definitely a systematic issue,” Rohan, who is pursuing MSc at IIT Delhi, expressed.Piyush described a similar experience. Workload varies sharply between departments, he said, in some, students can balance academics with other things; in others, "you have to keep doing one thing or another."&nbsp;The pressure is, very often, external. “Faculty here have immensely high expectations from students from the very beginning, and students, especially freshers are not used to that pressure. That becomes the breaking point for many,” he added.This is not just one student’s experience.In August 2024, IIT Delhi formed an expert committee to examine student suicides on campus, and recommend reforms in infrastructure and campus environment.The committee highlighted relentless academic pressure, unrealistic deadlines, weekend exams, and a grading system that could reinforce toxic competitiveness. It also flagged caste-based stereotyping, gender discrimination, and faculty-student friction.More importantly, the committee also highlighted a gap in the current mental-health facilities available on campus for students, including distrust in the counselling system.IIT Delhi student’s death | Police file abetment to suicide case against unidentified personsThe said recommendations were reportedly submitted in August 2024. IIT Delhi acknowledged its findings publicly only in April 2025, saying the factors identified had already been recognised internally and that a "comprehensive action plan" was being developed.By then, the institute had already seen another student death, in October 2024.Now, on August 22, 2026, another student has died on the IIT Delhi campus. renewing protests and calls for accountability. The institute has once again set up an inquiry committee, but students are not satisfied.Help is available, but often out of reach?IITs have expanded mental-health infrastructure significantly, including counsellors, psychiatrists, wellness centres, helplines, and peer-support systems. Data from IIT Madras says 3,366 students accessed counselling between 2019 and 2024 and it now offers 24x7 support for students. Similarly, IIT Kanpur has added psychiatrists and weekly psychiatric OPDs.In a recent response to student protest, IIT Delhi said that it has 24x7 counselling services, external mental-health support and an Academic Progress Group to identify students facing academic difficulties.But availability isn't the same as access, say students. "Is the administration here able to provide space for students to reach medical counselling in the first place? No, because there is no time." Rohan said.&nbsp;Piyush, on the other hand, recalled his own first year. "I was completely broken. I experienced anxiety for the first time, and I didn't expect it would become this difficult." He tried to access counselling but couldn't, slots were limited to certain days and times.&nbsp;"When you are mentally okay, you can think, 'There is a counsellor available, I should go talk to them.' But when you are actually struggling, you may not have the capacity to even think about whether someone is available," he said, highlighting that a lot of students often hesitate to approach a counsellor on campus due to fear of judgement and other reasons.Committees keep coming. What changes after them?The IITs, of course, have not been completely passive on the student deaths. After most of the recent student deaths, the administrations have formed inquiry committees and announced support for students as well as victim.Like at IIT Madras, an inquiry committee headed by retired IPS officer G Thilakavathi examined guide-student relationships, academic and personal pressures, support systems and grievance mechanisms after a series of deaths.Its recommendations included giving research scholars greater freedom in choosing guides, allowing students and guides to seek special Doctoral Committee meetings, introducing wellness surveys, providing additional monitoring for students with academic backlogs and strengthening parental support.In the case of PhD scholar Sachin Kumar Jain, a separate inquiry eventually resulted in the suspension of his supervisor, Professor Ashis Kumar Sen.IIT Delhi Director threatens disciplinary action against student protestorsSimilarly, at IIT Bombay, the death of first-year student Darshan Solanki in 2023 prompted an internal investigation and measures including recruitment of dedicated SC/ST counsellors and a committee to examine academic stress among first-year students.Similar committees have been formed across IITs and have recommended similar reforms. A lot of these reforms have been introduced, but gaps still remain.“The question should not be whether there is any infrastructure," Rohan said. "If there is infrastructure, and if you are such a great institute as you claim, why are these issues recurring again and again?” Rohan said.What happened this time?The questions have resurfaced once again, after 31-year-old MSc Physics student Rishikesh Kumar died at IIT Delhi on August 22 after falling from the sixth floor of the Lecture Hall Complex. As per olice reports, no suicide note was found, and the authorities have registered an FIR against unidentified persons on allegations of abetment of suicide.IIT Delhi said Kumar had received treatment and counselling support after concerns were raised about his health earlier this year. He was taken to a specialised hospital for about a month, his semester withdrawal requests were approved and the institute said it continued to provide him support after his return.Rohan*, Msc student, IIT DelhiSoon after the recent incident, the campus was running like nothing had happened... school students were being shown the library.”But students and Kumar’s family raised questions about his return to campus, alleging that he was not given hostel accommodation and faced difficulties in securing an academic project after returning from his medical break. These allegations are now part of the ongoing investigation.The death soon led to protests on campus, with students demanding an independent inquiry into Kumar’s death and alleged administrative lapses.But for students, the concern goes beyond just one incident. “Even after his death, things seemed to go back to normal very quickly, as if nothing had happened,” Piyush, a second-year BTech student, said.Rohan, an MSc student, recalled the days following Kumar’s death, “The campus was running like nothing had happened... school students were being shown the library.”For him, that points to a larger problem, the way repeated deaths can become seemingly normalised, he said.In March 2025, the Supreme Court also set up a National Task Force on Mental Health of Students and Prevention of Student Suicides and mandated to examine academic pressure, discrimination, harassment and institutional accountability.&nbsp;By February 2026, the Ministry of Education reported over 12.88 lakh student responses to its surveys.As students point out, IITs now have counsellors, monitoring systems and helplines in place. The bigger question, however, is whether students can actually access and use these systems when they need them most.

primary_source.headline: From Bill Gates to Bernie Sanders, most agree the AI arms race is disastrous. Only Europe can make it stop | Alexander Hurst
primary_source.content: An EU export ban on Dutch tech giant ASML’s machines could force the pause we all needAt this point, it should be clear that AI is a choose-your-own-adventure book where every option ends in disaster. Exploding carbon emissions and ecological collapse? Turn to page 37. Other outcomes include some or all of: the bubble bursting and an ensuing financial crisis; mass unemployment via automation; the end of democracy and the rise of authoritarian surveillance states; raving cults who believe the pattern-matching algorithm is a consciousness; terrorists who create devastating bioweapons; nation states that deploy autonomous weapons systems that act on non-human timeframes; nation states or terrorists that hack all the myriad systems we depend on; or an AI that, conscious or not, pursues directives that are at odds with human wellbeing.Imagining that people such as Elon Musk, the OpenAI boss, Sam Altman, Palantir’s Peter Thiel and the Trump administration tech adviser Marc Andreessen will lead us to a utopian future of flourishing environmentalism, social harmony and endless leisure requires hallucination and sycophancy so great that that choose-your-own-adventure scenario could only have been written by ChatGPT.Alexander Hurst writes for Guardian Europe from Paris. His memoir Generation Desperation is out now Continue reading...

Universities have defunded Diversity, Equity and Inclusion programmes, many media outlets have kowtowed to the US’s self-styled king and tech CEOs have jumped into bed with him. primary_source.headline: Explained | What is Quishing and how to safeguard yourself from such online fraud
primary_source.content: With wider availability of smartphones and computers, billions of people are online to work, consume multimedia content, play games, seek information for school project work, or for research studies.However, this also attracts criminals to prey on naive people, particularly senior citizens and young adults, who are just getting to know the internet and lack awareness of cyber threats. Quick summary - click for full detailsConcise summary of key highlightsExplained | What is Quishing and how to safeguard yourself from such online fraudIn one lineQuishing is a sophisticated QR code phishing scam bypassing email security to steal personal and financial data.Key points• What is QuishingQuishing is a phishing technique using malicious QR codes to redirect victims to compromised websites or download harmful content, bypassing traditional email security filters.• Sophistication levelQuishing is highly sophisticated, evading detection by secure email gateways like Google Gmail and Microsoft Outlook, which often treat QR codes as benign images.• Target demographicsCybercriminals primarily target senior citizens and young adults who are less aware of cyber threats, exploiting their trust and limited internet knowledge.• Primary risksThe ultimate goal of Quishing is to steal sensitive information such as passwords, financial data, Aadhaar card details, phone numbers, and bank credentials.• Prevention measuresUsers should avoid scanning unsolicited QR codes, install apps only from official stores, regularly update devices, and use reputable antivirus software.Key statistics7.4%Quishing as a percentage of malicious email detections in India11.2%JavaScript-based Trojan as a percentage of cyber threats detected30,000Mobile attacks blocked by Kaspersky in Q1 2026Processed with AI. Reviewed by DH Digital Team.Besides the usual phishing techniques such as sending compromised url links on emails and messenger apps, threat actors have come with new technique called QR Code Quishing.67% of India's Gen Z population feels confident online, but lack cybersecurity awareness: ReportAs per ESET's latest H1 2026 Threat Report, QR code phishing (quishing) has emerged as India's second-largest email threat, accounting for nearly 7.4 per cent of all malicious email detections. JavaScript-based Trojan is the top method, with 11.2 per cent of total cyber threat detection. That said, these Trojan malware-laced emails get detected fast if the user has an anti-virus app in the device.However, QR Quishing is growing out to be big new threat. So, what is it?As noted earlier, Quishing is a new type of phishing technique used by cyber criminals to hoodwink naive device owners scan a malicious QR Code and misdirect to a compromised website.This new Qushing technique is very sophisticated and can easily bypass conventional security screening by platforms such as Google Gmail, Microsoft Outlook and others.Regular emails get screened for URLs, which often get detected instantly. However, these QR codes in emails are perceived by many secure email gateways as benign images.Once this stage is passed, users believe it to be making the users vulnerable to specific forms of phishing attacks. QR codes can also be presented to intended victims in some other ways.QR codes can redirect victims to malicious websites or prompt them to download harmful content. Like all other phishing techniques, the ultimate goal is to steal private information, such as passwords, financial data, or personally identifiable information (PII) like Aadhaar card details, phone number, voter ID card number, house address, online bank account IDs and PIN credentials.Here's how to protect yourself from Quishing and other forms of online fraud1) Whenever you receive a call from a person identifying themselves as a police or Income Tax official, a cellular company executive or a bank official stating that your account may get seized, never panic. Just tell them, I will speak to a bank official and just cut the call. Go to the nearest bank branch and clear the doubt2) Regularly change the password of your netbanking account, both on the website and on the phone app3) If you ever receive messages with URL links or QR Codes to third-party app stores or websites or APK files resembling a bank app, ignore them. Never install an APK file shared on WhatsApp or any messenger or social media platform. For 99 per cent of the time, they are risky and potentially come with malware-laced files4) If you ever receive any cash prizes or job offers online, which look way too lucrative to be believable, then be wary of such rewards. They are likely a bait to reveal your personal information voluntarily; don't fall for this trick.5) Always install and download apps from the official Google Play Store, Microsoft Windows Store, and Apple App Store only6) Even if you are downloading from official websites or aforementioned platforms, make it a habit of reading the reviews of the app. The feedback shared by genuine users will let you know if the app is trustworthy or not.7) Ensure the device is fully updated to the latest version of the operating system. Smartphone, tablet and computer makers regularly send security patches along with OS updates to protect your device from such cyber threats8) Also, to be on the safe side, install anti-virus apps by renowned publishers such as Kaspersky, ESET and others. Kaspersky shared that it has blocked nearly 30,000 mobile attacks against consumers in the region during the first three months of 2026.In India, if you fall victim to online fraud, immediately call toll-free 1930. It is run by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre, and once you share the bank transaction details, they will be able to trace and freeze the mule bank accounts. Ensure you call them within one hour, as there will be a higher chance of blocking the cyber criminals from withdrawing the ill-gotten money.Digital Hygiene Tips: Here's how to safeguard yourself from mobile malware and cyber fraudGet the latest news on new launches, gadget reviews, apps, cybersecurity, and more on personal technology only on DH Tech.

stories.primary_headline: Think twice before installing this device promising free movies

primary_source.headline: Think twice before installing this device promising free movies
primary_source.content:
As online services get better at blocking malicious traffic, the attackers and scammers behind them have been forced to find new ways to reach their targets. The alternative of choice is now what are known as residential proxy networks. These systems funnel millions of home Internet connections into a unified network, and the proxy operators allow attackers to route their malicious traffic through these connections for a fee. The online services see only IP addresses with good reputations and geolocations that don’t stand out.
More often than not, the home users have no idea that their connections are being used to facilitate crime and occasionally even nation-state attacks. Users who do know often don’t care much. In exchange for leasing out part of their unlimited bandwidth to others, many get free movie and TV show streaming. Several less tech-savvy people I know who own such digital media players have told me, after I explain how the media players piggyback off their connections, that the bonanza of content is worth it. They find the tangible benefits outweigh the abstract harm they pose.
Infecting already compromised devices
Research published Monday brings the threat into much clearer view. Security firm Plume cataloged a vast ecosystem of malware that preys squarely on users of SuperBox, just one of many media players offering pirated content. These malicious apps can be surreptitiously installed by remote attackers even when the devices are positioned behind a router. While Monday’s deep-dive analysis focused exclusively on SuperBox, Plume warned that dozens of similar streaming devices pose precisely the same threat.Read full article

primary_source.headline: Sequoia-incubated Empirik launches with $21M to predict outages before they happen
primary_source.content: Empirik announced Tuesday that it is spinning out as an independent company after raising $21 million in seed funding from Sequoia, Canapi, and Alumni Ventures. By serving as an autonomous infrastructure engineer, Empirik allows busy DevOps and site reliability engineering teams to offload routine troubleshooting and focus on higher-value priorities. Since launching earlier this year, Empirik has already brought on customers ranging from startups to several Fortune 500 players, including S&P Global, Guardant Health, and a major consumer packaged goods (CPG) company. Empirik’s goal is to do for infrastructure engineers what Cursor and Claude Code did for software developers: automate certain tasks so they can work significantly faster. As AI accelerates the pace of software development, tools that help infrastructure engineers keep up with constant system changes are more vital than ever, Chandrayana told TechCrunch. “What agentic AI did for software, Empirik wants to do for infrastructure engineering,” he added.

stories.primary_headline: Pocket's AI made my game ideas real. Now Meta controls the results.

primary_source.headline: Pocket's AI made my game ideas real. Now Meta controls the results.
primary_source.content:
The relatively recent rise of AI-assisted coding tools and the whole concept of "vibe coding" have effectively upended entire software development workflows. While these tools have been available to novice coders willing to put in the work to set them up, those with little to no coding experience could still be a little put off by the CLIs, IDEs, and terminal-based tinkering needed to create a complex AI-coded project these days.
Meta's latest AI-based project launch wants to make that kind of vibe coding as instantly accessible as posting on social media. Pocket—which launched in the US last Friday, August 21, after Meta acquired the staff behind the now-defunct vibe-coding app Gizmo in March—is a mobile app that lets users create fully functional interactive "gizmos" just by typing prompts into a text box, without even the option to look at a line of code. Those gizmos can then be shared with the world in a TikTok-style endless scroll complete with likes, comments, reposts, and all the other hallmarks of social media addiction.
After playing around with Pocket for the better part of a week, I found myself getting hooked on the simple process of quickly standing up functional, relatively feature-rich game prototypes simply by chatting with an LLM. But the result of all that time and AI effort is a couple of interactive toys that are effectively trapped in Meta's new walled garden, without any real way to turn them into something separate.Read full article

primary_source.content: Good salary. Visa sponsored. Flight included. Applicants must be educated, fluent in English and confident online. It sounds like a great opportunity for a young graduate, but it is the bait in a trafficking operation. The advertised job does not exist. On arrival, the person’s passport is taken. They are moved to a compound they cannot leave and are forced to run online scams: impersonating strangers, building false relationships and persuading people thousands of kilometres away to send money. Those who miss their targets may be beaten, starved or placed in solitary confinement. Their families may sell land or take on debt to raise money to pay for their release. I heard versions of this story firsthand during a recent visit to Rwanda, where I met two survivors who had been trafficked through fraudulent job offers. They were fluent in English and comfortable with technology. They had been looking for the same thing as millions of other young people: a good job and the chance to build a better future. Those qualities made them valuable to the traffickers. They were given scripts and forced to impersonate women online, build romantic relationships with people in Europe and persuade them to send money.

stories.primary_headline: Inside Meta's push to put robots to work in data centers

primary_source.headline: Inside Meta’s push to put robots to work in data centers
primary_source.content:
Meta is testing robots that can plug in cables, reset servers, and handle other tasks inside its data centers, according to several current and former workers familiar with the projects. The ongoing effort, which has not been previously reported, may eventually allow Meta to operate its rapidly expanding data center footprint with fewer humans, keeping labor costs in check as its spending on AI infrastructure soars.
Meta is using robots and related hardware from several different vendors, including Watney Robotics, Kinova, and ABB, according to the same workers, who asked to remain anonymous because they weren’t authorized to speak to the media. Kinova and ABB declined to comment. Watney didn’t respond to requests for comment.
In one experiment, Meta is evaluating whether a Kinova Gen3 robotic arm could be used for power cycling or cutting off electricity to servers. The company is also testing a different robot to swap networking cables. One Meta data center worker estimates that if it’s successful, the bot could replace up to 80 percent of some people’s workloads. “We thought those of us performing the physical tasks were safe for a while, but not anymore,” says the worker. “It’s coming for us all, unfortunately.”Read full article

stories.primary_headline: This startup is fuel-injecting hydrogen to make cargo ships more efficient

primary_source.headline: This startup is fuel-injecting hydrogen to make cargo ships more efficient
primary_source.content: It’s one of the most iconic scenes in the Fast & Furious film franchise: Paul Walker’s thumb comes off the steering wheel and smashes a small red button, pumping nitrous oxide into the engine of his Mitsubishi Eclipse and giving the car an explosive boost. “Instead of getting power, we actually say to the engine: ‘Hey, reduce the fuel [flow] to the engine, we don’t need as much because we have some nitrous. It’s [just] called hydrogen,’” he told TechCrunch in an exclusive interview. The small team based in the San Francisco Bay Area has developed this hydrogen injection system as a retrofit, which it claims can be installed in less than two weeks without needing a dry dock. It cuts fuel use and emissions by more than 20%, and can save some vessels as much as $500,000 in annual costs, according to the startup. Newlight does this by constantly monitoring the diesel engine and finding optimal moments, down to the millisecond level, to inject the hydrogen fuel. That includes measuring exhaust temperature, combustion pressure, and air intake pressure, and increasing or decreasing the hydrogen flow every time a piston moves inside the engine’s cylinders. The startup says this hybrid system has completed its first long-range commercial voyage: an 8,500-nautical mile trip from Singapore to Ghana. Newlight installed its tech on a 650-foot-long Lomar Shipping bulk carrier ship for the test. The startup said its system reduced fuel consumption by 24% and carbon dioxide emissions by 28%. “It was amazing,” Haran Cohen Hillel, Cohen’s co-founder and the CEO of Newlight, said of the month-long voyage. “Being onboard and seeing the system operate in real conditions was a completely different experience from anything we had done in the lab.”

stories.primary_headline: Google Maps renames "Lake Ontario" to "Lake America" even faster than US government

primary_source.headline: Google Maps renames "Lake Ontario" to "Lake America" even faster than US government
primary_source.content:
Trade talks between the US and Canada broke down last week, leading to a wave of tariffs and retaliatory tariffs. US President Donald Trump also fell back on an old favorite to needle his opponents, signing an executive order on Thursday to rename Lake Ontario to "Lake America."
The body of water, which straddles the US-Canada border, gave its name to the Canadian province rather than the other way around. Regardless, the US government now refers to this great lake as Lake America—or it will soon. Official US government maps have yet to be updated, but Google wasted no time adopting the new, Trumpian name.
Google began rolling out this change for US users on Saturday. The company posted a brief update on its Google Maps blog, noting that it follows the US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) for its maps, so the company implies it had no choice but to rename Lake Ontario in Google Maps, which is the most popular mapping platform in the US by a wide margin.Read full article

stories.primary_headline: ChatGPT and Reddit now face EU's toughest online safety rules

primary_source.headline: ChatGPT and Reddit now face EU's toughest online safety rules
primary_source.content:
OpenAI’s ChatGPT will have to comply with tougher EU rules such as removing illegal content or face potential fines, the European Commission said on Monday, as Brussels grapples with how its existing digital regulation applies to rapidly evolving AI services.
The Commission said the chatbot, social media forum Reddit, and gaming platform Roblox would be classified as so-called very large online platforms under the EU Digital Services Act, its landmark online safety regime.
The designation means all three services will face additional obligations such as removing illegal content and protecting the privacy and security of minors and could face fines of up to 6 percent of their global revenue if they fail to comply.Read full article
